haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both return the same 401 login page with "Invalid email or password". Bcrypt runs against a fixed dummy hash when no user exists, so timing matches too.
haiku-low.q2: The lock check comes first. It returns 429 with Retry-After and login page. The password is not checked and no failure rows are written.
haiku-low.q3: The cookie's hash is read and its session row is deleted in the same transaction as the new session insert. The old session ends and a new ID is issued.
haiku-low.q4: Only the opaque random session ID, 32 bytes base64url, in cookie __Host-sid. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 hours after login. Each request extends the idle expiry by 30 minutes, but the absolute cap of created_at plus 12 hours is never extended.
haiku-low.q6: It returns 302 redirect to /login and clears the cookie. Unknown or expired sessions are never honored.
haiku-low.q7: It deletes the sessions row matching the cookie hash, then replies 303 to /login with a cleared cookie. If the session is already gone, the deletion removes nothing and the reply is the same.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sessions table, shared by both instances. Any instance finds it by the SHA-256 hash of the cookie value.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_failures table, one row per failed attempt per email. The server counts rows with failed_at within the last 10 minutes using Postgres now().
haiku-low.q10: It compares expires_at > now() in an UPDATE matching id_hash. It writes last_seen_at = now() and expires_at = least(now + 30 min, absolute_expires_at).
haiku-low.q11: It receives 503 "We can't sign you in right now. Try again in a minute." with no cookie. The transaction rolls back, so no session is created.
haiku-low.q12: A scheduled cleanup job every 5 minutes, which deletes sessions where expires_at <= now(). Correctness does not depend on it.

sonnet.q1: They don't differ. Both get a 401 login page with "Invalid email or password". Failures are recorded for unknown emails too, and bcrypt runs against a dummy hash for timing parity.
sonnet.q2: The lock was written when the fifth failure occurred (that fifth attempt still got a 401). Any later attempt, with any password, gets 429 with Retry-After and the login page while locked_until > now(). The password is not checked, no failure rows are written, and the lock is not extended. The lock lasts 15 minutes.
sonnet.q3: On successful login, the incoming cookie value is hashed with SHA-256. In the same transaction the session row with that hash is deleted and a new session row is inserted. A new ID is issued even if the old cookie was valid. If there is no cookie or no matching row, the delete removes nothing and login continues.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random session ID (32 CSPRNG bytes, base64url) in the cookie __Host-sid. No, page scripts cannot read it, because it is HttpOnly. It is also Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, with no Domain and no Max-Age.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after creation (login). The absolute cap, created_at + 12h, is never extended, even though each request refreshes the 30-minute idle expiry.
sonnet.q6: It responds 302 to /login with a cleared cookie (all attributes repeated with Max-Age=0). The UPDATE returns zero rows. A storage failure is different: 503 and the cookie is kept.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the sessions row for the cookie's hash before replying. Zero rows deleted is fine. If the session is already gone or there is none, the response is the same: 303 to /login with a cleared cookie. If storage fails, it returns 503 "We couldn't sign you out. Try again." and keeps the cookie.
sonnet.q8: In the Postgres sessions table (no Redis), which is the shared durable store for both instances. Either instance hashes the cookie value with SHA-256 and looks up and updates the row by id_hash (the primary key).
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_failures table, one row (email, failed_at) per failed attempt, indexed on (email, failed_at). The window is a sliding 10 minutes: the server counts rows for the normalized email with failed_at in the last 10 minutes, using Postgres now(). A count of 5 or more triggers the lock.
sonnet.q10: It matches id_hash and compares expires_at > now() (Postgres clock) in one atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING. When valid, it writes last_seen_at = now() and expires_at = least(now() + 30 min, absolute_expires_at), and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 "We can't sign you in right now. Try again in a minute." with no cookie set. The transaction rolls back, so no session, failure row or lock change is kept.
sonnet.q12: The scheduled cleanup job, every 5 minutes on either instance, which runs DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires_at <= now().
